L70:   * 【29†내과】
L71: 
L72: 서울대학교 동물병원의 임상시험 모집 공고를 안내해 드립니다.
L73: 
L74: 【43†Image】
L75: 
L76:   * ### 【44†Image】목적
L77: 
L78: 서울대학교 수의과대학 동물병원에서는 ELEKTA사의 최첨단 선형가속기 및 방사선 치료 전용소프트웨어MONACO 6.0을 도입하여 방사선 치료 프로토콜 정립 및 임상 데이터 확보를 위한 임상 시험을 아래와 같이 실시하고자 합니다.
L79: 
L80:   * ### 【44†Image】지원 자격
L81: 
L82: 다음 사항에 해당하는 환자에게 지원 자격이 주어집니다.
L83: (1) 본원에서 종양을 진료받고 있는 환자
L84: (2) 조직검사를 실시하였거나 그에 준한 검사를 실시하여 종양의 종류가 확인된 환자
L85: (3) 방사선치료 일정을 따를 수 있는 환자 (내원 일정 및 총 횟수는 종양마다 다양)
L86: (4) 치료 후 추적관찰 일정에 따를 수 있는 환자: 치료 후 30일, 90일, 180일에 내원
L87: (5) 전신 상태가 비교적 양호하여 일반적인 방사선치료에 적합한 환자
L88: (6) 종양의 진행이 급진적이지 않은 환자
L89: (7) 마취에 대한 유의적인 위험성이 없는 환자
L90: (8) 치료 정보의 학술적 사용에 동의하는 환자
L91: 
L92: 다음의 경우 임상시험 지원에서 제외됩니다.
L93: 
L94: - 임상적으로 방사선치료가 지시되지 않는 환자 (예: 전신 종양)
L95: - 기타 수의사의 판단에 따라 연구 참여에 부적절하다고 판단되는 경우
L96: - 각 부위별 일정 수의 환자만을 모집하므로 이미 해당 부위 지원자가 많을 경우
L97: 
L98: ※ 본 임상시험은 서울대학교 동물병원 내원 환자에 한해 실시하며 방사선치료만을 위해 초진 내원하는 경우 제외됩니다.
L99:   * ### 【44†Image】임상 시험 참가 혜택
L100: 
L101: - 방사선치료 및 추적검사 비용의 10% 할인 (VAT 포함) 혜택
L102: 
L103: * 불포함 사항: 입원비, 방사선치료와 관련 없는 증상의 검사 및 치료비
L104: 
L105:   * ### 【44†Image】임상 시험 일정 및 유의사항
L106: 
L107: 본 임상시험은 23.06.14 부터 24.12.13 까지 진행되며, 두부 및 복부, 사지 등 부위별 제한된 환자 (O마리)를 모집하므로 각 부위별로 모집이 조기 마감될 수 있습니다.
L108: 
L109: 병원 내원 일정은 환자마다 다르며 일반적으로 상담1회, 시뮬레이션 CT촬영 1회, 방사선 치료 (3-20회), 추적검사 (0일, 30일, 90일, 180일 차)로 진행됩니다.
L110: 
L111: 방사선치료는 통원 혹은 입원치료로 진행 가능하며, 입원비는 환자가 부담합니다.
L112: 
L113: 방사선치료 후 180일째 진행되는 추적검사까지 참가하는 것이 전체과정이며, 환자의 임상적 상태와 무관히 임의중단할 경우 혜택받은 치료비에 대해 반환하셔야 합니다.
L114: 방사선치료는 종양 뿐 아니라 정상 세포의 손상을 유발하므로 치료 부위에 따라 다양한 후유증이 동반될 수 있으며, 이에 대한 치료는 환자가 부담합니다.
L115: 
L116:   * ### 【44†Image】임상 시험 참가 방법
L117: 
L118: (1) 서울대학교 동물병원의 담당 주치의에게 요청하면 방사선종양팀에 연결됩니다.
L119: (2) 방사선종양팀에서 진료 기록 확인 후 적합한 환자로 판단되면 상담 일정을 잡아드립니다.

L20: Clinical trials and collaborative research in surgical oncology are actively encouraged by the VSSO. Prospective clinical trials are preferred, but multi-institutional retrospective case series will also be strongly considered. Research projects can include, but are not limited to, the study of new surgical techniques, multimodality treatment protocols, novel adjuvant agents, and treatment outcomes for different tumor types.

L41: # JUNE 2026
L42: 
L43: Evaluation of incidence and risk factors for surgical site infection following neoplastic canine limb amputations performed with and without a bipolar sealing device
L44: 
L45: Lead investigator: Andrea Erickson, DVM, DACVS-SA, ACVS Fellow – Surgical Oncology, EDUCT-MA (BME), Assistant Professor – Surgical Oncology and Soft Tissue Surgery, Oregon State University
L46: 
L47: Aim and objectives:
L48: The aim of this study is to evaluate the incidence and risk factors for surgical site infection (SSI) following neoplastic limb amputations performed with and without a bipolar vessel sealing device. Furthermore, we want to evaluate the influence of anesthetic and surgical time on SSI incidence for neoplastic limb amputations.
L49: 
L50: Please contact Dr. Erickson (erickand@oregonstate.edu) for more details.
L51: 
L52: * * *
L53: # OCTOBER 2025
L54: 
L55: Retrospective evaluation of impact of lymphadenectomy on survival of dogs with cutaneous mast cell tumors.
L56: 
L57: Lead investigator: Dr. Mirja Nolff (Clinic of Small Animal Surgery, Vetsuisse Zürich, University of Zürich, Switzerland).
L58: 
L59: Aim and objectives:
L60: The aim of this study is, to assess the impact of nodal management on outcome in dogs with grade 2/low grade mast cell tumors that are solely treated by surgical intervention. Furthermore, we want to assess if SLN based resection results in a superior outcome compared to regional lymphadenectomy. Our hypothesis is, that lymphadenectomy will result in improved survival time compared to cases were lymph-nodes were not treated in both species.
L61: Furthermore, we propose that this effect will be more pronounced in dogs when SLN mapping was used to determine the nodes to be resected.
L62: Please contact Dr. Nolff (mnolff@vetclinics.uzh.ch) for more details.
L63:

L65: # 2022
L66: ## The effects of lymph node extirpation on long-term prognosis of non-metastatic canine oral malignant melanoma.
L67: 
L68: Lead investigator: Dr. Judith Bertran
L69: 
L70: Aims and objectives of the study:
L71: 
L72:   1. To compare the disease progression rates, survival times of two treatment groups of nonmetastatic canine oral malignant melanoma (Stage I and Stage II with N0)— (1) primary tumor/local surgical excision (group 1) versus (2) primary tumor removal with non-selective cervical LNs extirpation (group 2).
L73:   2. To determine complications related to non-selective lymph node extirpation of the cervical
L74: 
L75: lymph nodes (> or = of 3 LNs).
L76: 
L77:   3. To evaluate the disease progression rate and survival times of a subgroup of dogs with OMM Stage I or II (with N0) that undergo a non-metastatic sentinel LN removal only.
L78: 
L79: We hypothesized that there would be a significant advantage of disease progression rates and survival times in the group where non-selective elective lymphadenectomy is performed.
L80: Please contact Dr. Bertran (bertran.judith@ufl.edu) for more details and for the data collection spreadsheet
L81:

L83: # 2021
L84: ## Outcomes and prognostic factors associated with surgical management of primary intramuscular hemangiosarcoma in dogs: A Veterinary Society of Surgical Oncology retrospective case series.
L85: 
L86: Lead investigators: Dr. Ronan A. Mullins and Dr. Michail Vagias
L87: 
L88: Objectives of the study:
L89: 1)    Describe the clinical outcome (progression free interval [PFI], recurrence rate and metastatic rate, and survival time [ST]) of dogs that underwent surgical excision (with or without adjuvant therapy) of primary intramuscular hemangiosarcoma (IMHSA).
L90: 
L91: 2)    Investigate factors associated with tumor recurrence and development of metastasis.
L92: 
L93: 3)    Investigate prognostic factors for progression free interval (PFI) and survival time (ST).
L94:

L96: # Closed RESEARCH TRIALS

L98: * * *
L99: ## The effects of adjuvant vs. sole therapy with Palladia (tocernib phosphate) in canine gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GIST’s) on long term survival.
L100: 
L101: Lead investigator: Judith Bertran
L102: 
L103: The main purpose of the proposed study is to compare the treatment of GIST’s with surgery alone versus in a microscopic setting treated with a full course of Palladia versus in a gross tumor setting with Palladia to determine if there is a clinical benefit to treating GISTs with Palladia
L104: 
L105: Aims:
L106: 1.To compare the disease progression rates and survival times of 3 treatment groups of Gastrointestinal Stromal Tumors (GISTs)— (1) surgery alone versus (2) surgery followed by Palladia (toceranib phosphate) versus (3) Palladia alone in a gross tumor setting.
L107: 2. To determine prognostic indicators associated with GISTs — previously described indicators of prognosis have not been consistent. These included mitotic index, tumor size, histopathologic subtype, and metastasis however these have not been consistent findings across all studies.
L108: 
L109: 3. To determine GIST associated clinical signs, signalment, and most common locations of tumor.
L110: 
L111: Please contact Dr. Bertran (bertran.judith@ufl.edu) for more details

L118: 
L119: Lead investigator: Dr. Sarah Boston (drsarahboston@GMAIL.COM)

L121: Aims and objectives:
L122: 
L123: 1.     To evaluate Soft Tissue Sarcomas that arise in the region of the Ischiatic Tuberosity as a distinct clinical entity
L124: 
L125: 2.     To evaluate outcome of surgical treatment
L126: 
L127: 3.     To evaluate factors that may influence DFI and ST after surgical treatment
L128: 
L129: 4.     Develop recommendations for resection, reconstruction and adjuvant therapy for canine buttock sarcomas
L130: Please contact Dr. Boston (drsarahboston@GMAIL.COM) for more details if needed and for the data collection spreadsheet.
